focus: Second tier of CI workflows: whether their cost is checkable work or plumbing, and whether any further cut exists
noveltyJustification: All 7 findings were new per-step measurements of six previously unexamined workflows plus the tier-level conclusion.
keyQuestions: Which CI workflows duplicate a local hook, another workflow, or a guard that fires no unique regression, and how many minutes does each remove per push or PR?
ruledOut: Telling these workflows to drop their checks
Recommending shallower clones for them (settled setup work)
Calling the trigger-index push job wasteful

graphEvents.label: Second tier: checks 10-66s against 96-188s of checkout plus install

label: gate-inputs costs 170s: 64s checkout, 34s install, 56s hook tests, 10s fixtures, so 66s is genuine checking work
trigger-index-rebuild costs 119s across 2 jobs, with a 32s job whose only task is pushing the rebuild and whose 25s is a base-commit checkout
opencode-dual-version costs 440s across 3 jobs: 183s checkout, 133s provisioning, 81s batteries, and the same 19s config-shape step runs twice
command-tree-parity costs 211s across 2 jobs: 120s checkout, 68s install, about 23s of comparison work
playbook-operator-contract costs 93s for under 8s of checking: 52s checkout and 31s install plus shared build
changed-packet-validation costs 129s for under 8s of validation: 79s checkout and 45s install
No second-tier workflow holds a deletable duplicate; their remaining ceiling is the settled setup and trigger work
